title: The Menstrual Cycle Phases
content: The menstrual cycle is generally divided into four phases: 1. Menstrual Phase (Days 1-5): The shedding of the uterine lining, which is your period. 2. Follicular Phase (Days 1-14): Starts on the first day of your period and continues until ovulation. The pituitary gland releases FSH to stimulate follicle growth in the ovaries. 3. Ovulation (Around Day 14): A mature egg is released into the fallopian tube. 4. Luteal Phase (Days 15-28): The ruptured follicle becomes the corpus luteum, producing progesterone to thicken the uterine lining for potential pregnancy. If no fertilization occurs, hormone levels drop, triggering menstruation.
